findings.problem: The four `have` blocks at lines 84–101 (haU, hcU, haV, hcV) are verbatim copies of the two bullets at lines 38–44 in `polynomialLogDerivative_mem_of_coefficients`. Each copy performs the same nontrivial chain: rewrite `polynomialFirstJetHom` to `dualEvalLie` on the coordinate, use `dualEvalLie_base` / `dualEvalLie_tangent` to turn the dual-component into `eval t A.coord` / `eval t (directionalDerivative h A.coord)`, and then recover membership from coefficient membership via `eval_mem_iff_coefficients`, the tangent case additionally composing with `directionalDerivative_mem_coefficientSubmodule`. The block for `A` occurs three times (lines 38–44, 84–87 and 92–96) and the block for `C` twice (88–91, 97–101), so any change to the invariant-membership argument (for instance a change in the `dualEvalLie_base`/`tangent` normal form, or in the way derivative invariance is transported) must be made in five places.
findings.proposed_change:
Extract one helper in `NilpotentLieBCHGroup` next to `polynomialFirstJet_coord`, e.g.

```lean
theorem polynomialFirstJet_coord_mem (U : LieSubalgebra ℚ L) (V : Submodule ℚ L)
    (A : PolynomialGroup σ hnil)
    (hAU : ∀ α, coefficients A.coord α ∈ U)
    (hAV : ∀ α, coefficients A.coord α ∈ V) (t h : σ → ℚ) :
    dualBaseLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h A).coord ∈ U ∧
      dualTangentLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h A).coord ∈ V := by
  constructor
  · change dualBaseLinear (dualEvalLie t h A.coord) ∈ U
    rw [dualEvalLie_base]
    exact (eval_mem_iff_coefficients U.toSubmodule A.coord).mpr hAU t
  · change dualTangentLinear (dualEvalLie t h A.coord) ∈ V
    rw [dualEvalLie_tangent]
    exact (eval_mem_iff_coefficients V _).mpr
      (directionalDerivative_mem_coefficientSubmodule V h A.coord hAV) t
```

Then `polynomialLogDerivative_mem_of_coefficients` becomes
`obtain ⟨hbase, htangent⟩ := polynomialFirstJet_coord_mem U V A hAU hAV t h; exact dualLogDerivative_mem_of_invariant U V hUV _ hbase htangent`,
and in `polynomial_removal_preserves_derivative_layers` the four `have`s collapse to
`obtain ⟨haU, haV⟩ := polynomialFirstJet_coord_mem U V A hAU hAV t h` and
`obtain ⟨hcU, hcV⟩ := polynomialFirstJet_coord_mem U V C hCU hCV t h`, feeding `haU hcU haV hcV` to `F.derivative_removal_preserves_quotient_layers` exactly as the hypotheses require. The helper only uses imports already present in the file and the `[Fintype σ]` supplied by the section variables; this has not been checked by compilation.
findings.benefit: The argument relating coefficient membership of `A.coord` to membership of both components of the first jet — the mathematical heart shared by both theorems — would live in a single, named, independently readable lemma with its own statement of hypotheses. Readers of the layer-removal theorem would see the reduction to `derivative_removal_preserves_quotient_layers` without re-reading five copies of the same `change`/`rw`/`eval_mem_iff_coefficients` chain, and future changes to the `dualEvalLie` API would need to be fixed once rather than in five places (including inside `polynomialLogDerivative_mem_of_coefficients`, where the two bullets would otherwise silently diverge from the copies below).

theorem dualEvalLie_tangent [Fintype σ] (t h : σ → ℚ) (p : VectorPolynomial σ ℚ L) :
    dualTangentLinear (dualEvalLie t h p) = eval t (directionalDerivative h p) := by
